<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

V4.1 DSML markers contain a dedicated `｜DSML｜` token surrounded by ordinary text. The parser currently also accepts copies spelled entirely with ordinary tokens, turning quoted examples into tool calls or cutting reasoning and string arguments short. This change requires token provenance for DSML structure when output token IDs are available.

This is output-side work, distinct from input sanitization in #62667. #50676 and #60256 overlap with non-streaming token-ID handling; neither covers the streaming reasoning-to-tool hand-off here. #59145 addresses token-aware structural tags, a remaining compatibility gap below. #62517 and #61142 extend opener variants in the same format; they do not add this provenance guard.

## Claims

- With token IDs, ordinary-token DSML copies stay text in content, reasoning and string arguments, in streaming and non-streaming. Genuine markers retain their positions across split UTF-8 characters, held-back text and reasoning-to-tool transitions; they cannot bind to a later text copy.
- The tool parser's guard works with or without the reasoning parser. Unified reasoning/tool routing requires auto tools and both `deepseek_v41` parsers. On that route, requests without tools and `tool_choice="none"` return DSML call markup as content instead of silently dropping it, even without token IDs.
- In token-ID mode, text between and after tool-call blocks is returned as content, in order. Prompt-state detection stops at assistant, user and system role boundaries: a prompt that closes reasoning starts in content; an earlier turn's closing marker cannot disable reasoning in a new task prompt.
- Without token IDs, DSML matching remains text-based. Configurations without composite terminals retain their existing token-scanning paths.

## Validation

Validation uses the real V4.1 tokenizer and vLLM's incremental detokenizer on macOS CPU.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `tests/tool_parsers/test_deepseekv41_tool_parser.py` + `tests/parser/engine/test_token_id_scanner.py` | 183 passed |
| The 15 regression cases added for the review follow-up, against the previous revision of this change | 15 failed (decode reuse, composite variant without atom, task prompt state) |
| Replay, `--parser-class manager` / `--parser-class direct` | 130/130 / 130/130 |
| `pre-commit run --files <changed>` (ruff, mypy, typos, test tethering) | Pass |

Per-delta parser cost (`parse_delta`, 1,361 prose tokens plus a tool-call tail, median of seven runs):

| | `main` | previous revision | this revision |
|---|---|---|---|
| prose delta, median | 7.3 us | 19.0 us | 13.8 us |
| whole stream | 24.4 ms | 42.2 ms | 31.9 ms (1.31x `main`) |

```bash
export PYTHONPATH=$PWD PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1
python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider \
  tests/tool_parsers/test_deepseekv41_tool_parser.py \
  tests/parser/engine/test_token_id_scanner.py -q
```

The replay covers 26 synthetic outputs under five delta schedules, separately through manager and direct parser construction. The benchmark streams 1,361 prose tokens followed by a tool-call tail, measures `parse_delta`, and reports median/p95 delta times and the median whole-stream time over seven repetitions. No sweep or full suite is required for this follow-up.

Coverage includes ordinary-token copies, real-marker/text-copy twins, parameter boundaries, implicit and explicit reasoning ends, held-back detokenization, disabled tools, prompt state and required/named request adjustment. The forced-choice cases do not prove that a string-based constrained decoder cannot sample split marker spellings.

**Outstanding:** no serving regression, Responses API test or model evaluation was run. This CPU-only environment cannot serve the model; no small checkpoint sharing its tokenizer was available. Parser tests exercise serving-layer parser construction, not HTTP. CI runs `tests/tool_parsers`, but its `tests/parser` step is commented out; scanner cases require local execution.

## Details

**Root cause.** Composite DSML markers do not resolve to one token ID, so text matching bypasses the engine's protection for dedicated-token terminals. Searching text for token spellings can also rebind a genuine marker to a later copy. Separate reasoning and tool engines lose provenance at the hand-off, and non-streaming delegation does not forward output IDs.

**Mechanism.** `composite_token_id_terminals` declares each marker's required token atom. Scanner alignment produces trusted spans for the lexer, parameter conversion and open-value extension. Unaligned text stays buffered, then falls back to content at end-of-stream without trusting markers. Full ByteLevel runs with exact byte counts avoid redundant decoding unless replacement characters make counts ambiguous; one-token runs reuse the decode cache. Partial prefixes still require decoded alignment. Span mode bypasses the normal plain-content fast path; the remaining cost is in the table above.

**Routing and scope.** The V4.1 wrapper shares one reasoning/tool engine, retaining request adjustment and constrained-JSON dispatch. This preserves streaming provenance and forwards non-streaming IDs, overlapping #50676/#60256. Span tracking is generic and opt-in. Post-call content and deferred-content ordering remain gated by composite-terminal mode in shared engine files: a design tradeoff, not a general routing cleanup. Prompt boundaries are configured in V4.1; its streaming hook still applies the base prompt-state calculation because the base hook is a no-op.

**Structural-tag limitation.** Strict required/named choices use string-based structural tags. A forced call whose DSML atom is sampled as ordinary tokens would be returned as content, potentially yielding no tool call. This is inferred from the grammar/parser interaction, not reproduced with constrained model generation. There is no mitigation in this PR: token-aware tags in #59145 are the preferred direction; a future request-scoped guard bypass for constrained output is another option.

**Other limits.** Custom detokenizers whose text never aligns with IDs fall back to text. Streaming still drops a whitespace-only content delta immediately after a call, as before. No end-to-end latency or throughput improvement is claimed.

+"""DeepSeek V4.1 output parsing through ParserManager with the real tokenizer.
+
+The V4.1 tokenizer spells each DSML marker as ordinary text around the
+``｜DSML｜`` token, so the model can also write any marker with ordinary
+tokens. Only markers whose ``｜DSML｜`` arrived as the token are structure.
+"""

+import json
+import os
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import textwrap
+
+import pytest
+
+from vllm.entrypoints.openai.chat_completion.protocol import ChatCompletionRequest
+from vllm.parser.parser_manager import ParserManager
+from vllm.tokenizers import get_tokenizer
+from vllm.tokenizers.detokenizer_utils import detokenize_incrementally
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skip_global_cleanup
+
+MODEL = "deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash"
+ATOM = "｜DSML｜"
+THINK_START_ID = 128821
+THINK_END_ID = 128822
+CALL = (
+    '<｜DSML｜ calls><｜DSML｜ invoke name="calc">'
+    '<｜DSML｜ parameter name="value" string="false">42</｜DSML｜ parameter>'
+    "</｜DSML｜ invoke></｜DSML｜ calls>"
+)
+TWIN = CALL.replace(">42<", ">99<")
+INVOKE = CALL.removeprefix("<｜DSML｜ calls>").removesuffix("</｜DSML｜ calls>")
+STRING_HEAD = (
+    '<｜DSML｜ calls><｜DSML｜ invoke name="echo">'
+    '<｜DSML｜ parameter name="text" string="true">'
+)
+STRING_TAIL = "</｜DSML｜ parameter></｜DSML｜ invoke></｜DSML｜ calls>"
+CALC = ("calc", {"value": 42})
+TOOLS = [
+    {
+        "type": "function",
+        "function": {
+            "name": name,
+            "parameters": {
+                "type": "object",
+                "properties": {key: {"type": kind} for key, kind in props},
+            },
+        },
+    }
+    for name, props in (
+        ("calc", [("value", "integer")]),
+        ("echo", [("text", "string"), ("note", "string")]),
+    )
+]
+SCHEDULES = ["nonstream", "one_chunk", "per_token", "text_lag3"]
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
+def tokenizer():
+    return get_tokenizer(MODEL, tokenizer_mode="deepseek_v41")
+
+
+def marker_ids(tokenizer, text):
+    ids = tokenizer.encode(text, add_special_tokens=False)
+    assert tokenizer.convert_tokens_to_ids(ATOM) in ids
+    return ids
+
+
+def text_ids(tokenizer, text):
+    """Spell *text* with ordinary tokens only, as the model can."""
+    added = set(tokenizer.get_added_vocab().values())
+    ids = []
+    for token_id in tokenizer.encode(text, add_special_tokens=False):
+        if token_id not in added:
+            ids.append(token_id)
+            continue
+        for ch in tokenizer.decode([token_id]):
+            ids += tokenizer.encode(ch, add_special_tokens=False)
+    assert added.isdisjoint(ids) and tokenizer.decode(ids) == text
+    return ids

+        tool_parser_name="deepseek_v41",
+        reasoning_parser_name="deepseek_v41",

In short: the V4.1 parser accepts DSML markers spelled with ordinary tokens. A model quoting a tool-call example, or a user pasting one, then gets a real tool call, and reasoning or string arguments can be cut short. With this PR, DSML counts as structure only when its `｜DSML｜` part arrived as the dedicated token (id 128825). I run an equivalent patch on a V4.1-Flash deployment. Tests, replay and parser cost are in the description.

The diff is about +1.3k lines. If smaller pieces are easier to review, I have it split locally into three stacked PRs:

1. One serving engine for V4.1 reasoning and tool parsing: token IDs survive the reasoning-to-tool hand-off and reach non-streaming parsing; DSML stays content when tools are absent or `tool_choice="none"`.
2. The token-provenance guard for DSML markers.
3. Content order around tool calls, and prompt reasoning state at turn boundaries.

The production code at the end of the stack is the same as in this PR. Either way works for me, tell me which you prefer.
